item.name: Ingest
item.description:
Getting events in. Three paths, one normalizer: a single JSON event, an
NDJSON batch from the collector, and a whole vendor export file.

description.content:
Accepts one vendor event as JSON, normalizes it, and stores it. The
event is committed before this call returns, so it is searchable
immediately.

A body that is not a JSON object is answered with 400 `invalid_json`.
An event that is JSON but cannot be stored is answered with 200, and
`errors[0]` says why, as it would for a line of a batch. The body may
be at most 1 MiB.

Caddy exposes this as `POST /ingest` at the edge, which is the form
the sample senders use.

event reports why in `errors[0]`.

item.name: Ingest a batch of events as NDJSON

request.name: Ingest a batch of events as NDJSON

description.content:
One JSON event per line. This is what the collector forwards after
buffering syslog and file input.

A malformed or unmappable line does not fail the request: the response
reports `accepted` and `rejected` counts with per-line detail. This is
deliberate — the collector retries any non-2xx response from its disk
buffer, so rejecting a whole batch for one poison line would retry it
forever and stall the buffer behind it. A non-2xx status here means the
request was unusable as a whole, not that some records were bad.

Blank lines are skipped and are not records. A line may be at most
1 MiB, and the body at most 32 MiB.

description.content:
Same wire format and same per-record error handling as the batch
endpoint, for uploading a vendor export directly:

```
curl -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' \
     --data-binary @samples/json/aws_cloudtrail.ndjson \
     https://localhost/api/v1/ingest/file
```

`tenant` and `source` may be supplied as query parameters, and apply
only to records that do not carry their own.

Filtered, time-ordered list of normalized events.

Results are paged with an opaque cursor rather than an offset. Events
arrive continuously, so an offset would shift under the reader between
pages, showing duplicates and silently skipping rows. Pass the
`next_cursor` from one response as `cursor` on the next request; its
absence means there are no more results.

A cursor is tied to the filters it was produced with. Re-using one with
different filters is rejected with `invalid_cursor` rather than
silently paging through a different result set. `from` and `to` may be
left out after the first page; the cursor remembers the window.

Any other unusable parameter is rejected with `invalid_parameter`. A
search still running after 10 seconds, usually a free-text one over a
wide window, is cancelled with 503 `search_timeout`.

enforced beneath the API by row-level security.

Omitting it is always safe and is the common case — it returns

omitting it currently returns every tenant.

Multi-tenant log management: ingest events from many sources, normalize them
into one schema, and search them.

## Shape of this API

Ingest is permissive and search is strict. A sender may post whatever its
vendor emits; unknown fields are preserved verbatim in `raw` and stay
searchable. What comes back out of search is the normalized schema, with
every field named as in the common event schema.

## Errors

Every error is the same JSON envelope: a stable `code` to match on, a
human `message` that may change, and `request_id` correlating with the
server log. `422` additionally carries per-field failures in `errors[]`;
no other status does.

A `404` or `405` from an unrouted path is generated by the Go HTTP mux and
is plain text rather than this envelope.

## Not yet implemented

This is the first slice. Authentication is not wired up: no endpoint
currently requires a credential, and `tenant` is taken from the request
rather than from a verified token. Both change in the auth milestone, and
the affected fields say so individually.
